decision.recommended_plan: No tension between the two agents' recommendations. Cost recommends phasing the total day-one gap of 173,062.78 USD 50/50 across two phases (86,531.39 USD each) due to concentration of cost in a handful of large gaps (notably NYX-007 and NYX-013, which together are ~58% of the total). Retention independently identifies NYX-007 and NYX-013 as the only underwater employees (compa-ratios 0.76 and 0.77, both below the 0.85 threshold) but explicitly declines to designate either as "critical" -- their L3 level and role descriptions ("strong contributor," "picking up more responsibility") don't meet the bar for organizational criticality that would require day-one funding to prevent flight risk. Since retention flagged zero critical employees, there is no critical-underwater employee whose retention need would be left unmet during the phased gap. The phasing conflict pattern (critical + underwater employee exposed during an unfunded interim period) simply doesn't arise here. Recommended plan: adopt cost's phased schedule as proposed -- phase 1 at 86,531.39 USD and phase 2 at 86,531.39 USD, split evenly per comp_philosophy.md's standard [0.5, 0.5] schedule. This phasing applies uniformly to the pay-gap remediation for NYX-006, NYX-007, NYX-012, NYX-013, and NYX-016 (the five employees with nonzero cost_gap), and separately, if retention awards are pursued, the same phased structure applies to the 76,688.80 USD total award for NYX-007 and NYX-013. Both agents' figures can be executed on the phased timeline without leaving any critical person underwater in the interim, since no one was flagged as critical. If new information later surfaces establishing NYX-007 or NYX-013 as holding singular technical ownership, sole-specialist status, or leadership scope, retention's criticality assessment -- and by extension the case for accelerating their phase-1 funding -- should be revisited.
